# React runtime, switching, and subscriptions

## Language switcher

```tsx
import { t } from '@fluentic/i18n';
import { I18nManager, I18nState } from '@fluentic/i18n-web';
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

export function LanguageSwitcher() {
  const state = I18nState.use();
  const [failed, setFailed] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    document.documentElement.lang = state.languageId;
  }, [state.languageId]);

  async function change(languageId: string) {
    try {
      setFailed(false);
      await I18nManager.setLanguageId(languageId);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Language switch failed', error);
      setFailed(true);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <label htmlFor='language'>{t.jsx('Language')}</label>
      <select
        id='language'
        value={state.languageId}
        disabled={state.isLoading}
        onChange={(event) => void change(event.target.value)}
      >
        <option value='en'>English</option>
        <option value='fr'>Français</option>
      </select>
      {failed && <p role='alert'>{t.jsx('Could not load translations. Please try again.')}</p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Language commits only after required catalogs load. Failure leaves the old language active. Successful changes persist when `createLocalStorage()` is configured.

## Reactivity choices

`t.jsx(message)` returns a provider-aware element and subscribes internally:

```tsx
<h1>{t.jsx('Dashboard')}</h1>
```

`I18nState.use()` rerenders the whole component. Use it for many `t.text()` calls or when reading `{languageId, isLoading, ready}`:

```tsx
function Form() {
  I18nState.use();
  return <input placeholder={t.text('Email address')} />;
}
```

`t.jsx(() => element)` reruns one element callback without rerendering the parent:

```tsx
function Form() {
  return t.jsx(() => (
    <input placeholder={t.text('Email address')} />
  ));
}
```

The callback returns exactly one React element. It must contain no hooks. Nested messages are normal extraction/compiler markers.

## Outside React

Read a snapshot:

```ts
const { languageId, isLoading, ready } = I18nState.get();
```

Subscribe and clean up:

```ts
const updateTitle = () => {
  document.title = t.text('Your workspace');
};

updateTitle();
const unsubscribe = I18nState.subscribe(updateTitle);
// Later: unsubscribe();
```

Do not store a translated string at module scope; format it when used.

## Isolated providers

`createI18nManager()` returns an isolated `{manager, state, runtime}`. Initialize it, then pass it to `I18nProvider`. `t.jsx()` and the callback boundary discover the provider. For component-level string rendering, use `useI18nRenderer(t.text)`.

SPA code does not use `getSnapshot()` or `hydrate()`. Those live at `@fluentic/i18n/hydration` for SSR adapters; Next.js handles them internally.
